Package com.privatechain.network.peer

Class Peer

java.lang.Object
com.privatechain.network.peer.Peer
public final class Peer extends Object
Immutable value object representing a remote peer node in the private blockchain network.

A Peer encapsulates all the addressing and identity information needed to establish and maintain a TCP connection to another network participant. It is used by PeerManager to track the set of known nodes and by NodeClient to open outbound connections (design.md §3, FR-NET-01).

Identity vs address

The nodeId is a stable logical identifier (e.g., a hex-encoded public key hash) that persists across reconnections. The host/port pair is the current physical location of the peer, which may change if the peer restarts on a different address.

Usage


 Peer peer = Peer.builder()
     .nodeId("ab12cd34ef56...")
     .host("192.168.1.10")
     .port(8545)
     .publicKeyHex("04aabb...")
     .build();

 // Record a heartbeat
 Peer refreshed = peer.withLastSeen(Instant.now());
Since:
1.0.0

    • withLastSeen

      public Peer withLastSeen(Instant lastSeen)
      Returns a new Peer with the lastSeen field updated to the given instant.

      All other fields are carried over unchanged. This method is used by PeerManager on every successful heartbeat or message exchange.

      Parameters:
      lastSeen - updated last-seen timestamp (non-null)
      Returns:
      new Peer instance with updated timestamp
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if lastSeen is null

    • withPublicKey

      public Peer withPublicKey(String publicKeyHex)
      Returns a new Peer with the public key filled in after handshake.
      Parameters:
      publicKeyHex - hex-encoded secp256k1 public key (non-null, non-blank)
      Returns:
      new Peer instance with populated public key
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if publicKeyHex is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if publicKeyHex is blank
